summary.intent: Bootstrap release-please with correct version tags after phase 41 introduced a versioning and release system, and validate the system with a real quick task (exposing API version on /health endpoint).
summary.outcome: Release-please was bootstrapped with 15 version tags, the api-client versions were aligned to match the API version, the /health endpoint now returns the API version, and the PR release preview workflow was restructured to write release-as targets to the PR branch instead of pushing directly to main (avoiding branch protection issues). Several CI/release pipeline bugs were fixed along the way.

repo: release-please extra-files paths are relative to the package directory, not the repo root — apps/api extra-files must use ../../packages/api-client/openapi.json not packages/api-client/openapi.json
The OpenAPI spec version was hardcoded as 0.1.0 in both main.ts and generate-openapi.ts and was never updated from initial default

HealthController is excluded from the OpenApiGeneratorModule because it depends on TypeOrmHealthIndicator requiring a real DB connection — a manual spec definition exists in generate-openapi.ts instead
Phase 41 discussion log (41-DISCUSSION-LOG.md) specified monotonic major.minor versioning for web and desktop apps, but implementation defaulted to semver; this was accepted as-is
The pr-release-preview.js workflow processes all PR commits including merge commits, which caused false release labels when a merge commit brought in version bump changes from a release PR
release-please does not have a built-in monotonic versioning mode

The post-merge-release.yml workflow tried to push release-as targets directly to main but failed due to branch protection rules; this was resolved by moving the logic to the PR preview workflow instead

code.finding: Version reading moved to shared src/version.ts module; uses process.env.npm_package_version with fallback to reading package.json directly
Imports API_VERSION from shared src/version.ts instead of duplicating version-reading logic
New shared module that exports API_VERSION constant, reads from npm_package_version env var or package.json fallback
OpenAPI version now reads from npm_package_version env var with fail-fast if missing, replacing hardcoded 0.1.0
Merge commits (2+ parents) must be filtered out before conventional commit parsing to avoid false release labels
When existing higher-or-equal release label is treated as manual override, packageBumps must be updated to reflect the preserved label so release-as derivation uses the correct bump level
release:none should clear stale release-as entries only for keys this PR introduced (by comparing against base branch config snapshot), not entries set by previously merged PRs
bump-minor-pre-major config must be applied when computing release-as targets for 0.x packages on breaking changes
extra-files with jsonpath for packages/api-client/openapi.json must be on root package (.) not apps/api, since paths are relative to the package directory

workflow: When release-please is first set up with no prior tags, it treats entire commit history as unreleased — bootstrap by creating version tags at the commit before setup
Use chore(ci): not fix: for CI/tooling changes to avoid triggering unwanted release-please version bumps
GitHub Actions GITHUB_TOKEN pushes don't trigger new workflow runs (recursion prevention built-in), so PR preview workflows can safely commit back to PR branches

Legacy branch protection rules don't support per-actor bypass; Repository Rulesets do but have had issues in this repo — the practical alternative is to have CI commit to the PR branch and let the PR merge carry changes to main
The Verify API Spec & Client CI check regenerates the OpenAPI spec and diffs it — any committed openapi.json that doesn't match what the generator produces at the bumped version will fail this check

friction: post-merge-release.yml failed because github-actions[bot] can't bypass branch protection on main — wasted time trying to grant bypass permissions before restructuring the approach
Cargo.lock update via cargo update pulled in many unrelated dependency changes; had to use targeted workspace-only update instead
git index.lock stale file blocked git operations and required manual removal
fix: commit prefix (used for addressing review comments) triggered release-please version bumps; had to rewrite commit history with force push to change to chore(ci):
release-please extra-files relative path behavior was non-obvious, causing openapi.json to not be bumped in release PRs
PR #431 self-test via the preview workflow revealed multiple edge cases requiring several rounds of review comment resolution
PR #430 release gate blocked by Web E2E test flakiness from a prior run that wasn't re-run
open_items: PR #432 (fix release-please extra-files path for openapi.json) needs to merge and then PR #430 release PR needs to be regenerated
PR #430 release PR changelog needs to be re-evaluated after extra-files path fix lands — openapi.json should now be bumped to 0.36.0 automatically
Consider whether the Verify API Spec & Client check needs to handle release PR branches specially (where package.json is bumped but openapi.json hasn't been regenerated yet)
Phase 41 discussion log specified monotonic versioning for web/desktop but semver was implemented — deferred as acceptable for now, revisit if needed

The generate-openapi.ts HealthController manual spec was added but the /health endpoint schema completeness (details, error fields) was fixed mid-session — verify the final schema matches the actual controller response shape
